own_solution.law: Snell's law n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2)
assumptions: light goes from n=1 into n=1.5, so no total internal reflection

defect_reasons.other: TE757's 'Before the refraction was observed ... had grown by 11 degrees' admits a minority reading in which 40 degrees is the incidence at observation (answer 25.37) rather than the pre-tilt value (answer 31.20, as certified); the intended reading is the more natural one, so this is a wording issue rather than a wrong claim.

notes: Checked certified answers: theta1=46 deg: sin46/1.5 = 0.47956, theta2 = 28.657 deg; theta1=51: 0.51810, theta2 = 31.205; theta1=54: sin54/1.5 = 0.53934, theta2 = 32.639; base 40: 25.374. All match. Relation, inputs and units are consistent; all values stay below the incidence limit of 90 deg and no TIR arises (n1<n2). Strata agree with my pass 1. T7ECD/TE757 form a proper minimal pair (same 11 deg, attached to an earlier experiment vs to the present one before observation). T5D5A vs T43D0 are correctly declared not a minimal pair. In pass 1 I flagged rendering_not_minimal for T5A16 and T2905 lacking a number; the pass-2 claims declare these as numeral-free controls by design (twins of T7ECD and T5D5A), not as same-number variants, so I withdraw that flag here. The scene clause (camera) is harmless and has no physical path to the target.
